title: Anyone see all three? #musicaltheatre #theatre #theodyssey #broadway
transcript: Did you know there have been three musicals about Penelope from the Odyssey just in the last few years? And I mean specifically about Penelope, not [the Odyssey overall, like in Epic musical. The one I generally hear people talk about most is “Penelope, an epic new musical” This one starred Grace McLean as a one woman musical, and the score was by Alex Bechtel. I believe this one premiered in 2023, and it's been performed a number of times since, and there's a live cast album. But the year before that, there was also “Penelope, or how the Odyssey was really written,” which was a more comedic take on Penelope's story by David Weiner and Peter Kellogg. This one played at the York Theatre off Broadway in 2022, and I don't believe it's really been performed much since. There is a cast album, which I listen to *some* of, if I'm being honest, and, uh, I wouldn't say it was for me. But even before that was a sort of experimental music theatre piece co written by Tom Stoppard and Andre Previn. I believe this one had its world premiere in 2019, but I saw it in 2022 at Carnegie Hall, starring Uma Thurman and Renee Fleming. The concept behind this one is that they were kind of both and Penelope, but they would alternate between spoken monologues and sung arias. And I think it kind of represented Penelope's internal battle between cynicism and optimism for Odysseus. this is actually, the only one of the three that I personally saw. And I guess the only one to be, traditionally dramatized, is the one at the York Theatre, whereas the other two were more like monologues. But from the impressions I have of all three, it does seem like this one was the best by far. It's also the only one written by women.
